kind: full conversations, two paired arms (official tau2 grade); alltools; billed budget accounting
question: On development tasks that strong standard agents solve, does harness v3.1 (v1's checks + capability search + the once-only, explicit transfer hold) make gpt-5-mini complete more of them than the benchmark's standard agent, with identical settings?
supersedes: H007 (frozen at 7a3627d, never run). H007's treatment was v3. Before it ran, research/literature found that v3's give-up check would hold 16 of 23 correct transfers by the public top agents on the three tasks here that pass only with a transfer, and that in our runs a held transfer was never executed later (0 of 25); in every held transfer we can replay (9 of 9, H004) the agent then told the customer a transfer was under way. v3.1 changes only that hold (research/v3_1/README.md). Tasks, attempts, order, settings, budget and the gate are H007's. H006 (frozen, never run) stays superseded.
disclosure: The v3.1 change was motivated by evidence that includes three of these tasks: their reward basis and reference actions (a transfer is required on task_004, task_012 and task_035), and the public top agents' conversations on them (development tasks). The change itself names no task, document or tool other than transfer_to_human_agents. We have no gpt-5-mini conversation on nine of the twelve tasks; on task_089, task_058 and task_023 we have the pilots (H002-H005). This is a development result either way; the held-out split is untouched.
arms_note: 'baseline' is tau2's standard LLMAgent, unmodified. 'harness_v3_1' is bench/harness.py with {"version": "v3.1"}. Dependency search is off; v2 is not used.
selection_rule: The 12 development tasks that BOTH public top standard agents (GPT-5.5 xhigh and Qwen 3.8 Max, alltools, 4 trials each) passed at least 3 times of 4 (research/public_trajectories/analyze.py). The rule uses other models' public results, not our own outcomes, and is fixed before any run. Reason: on the other dev tasks even those agents almost never pass (9 tasks: 0 of 8), so a comparison there cannot show an improvement. The held-out split is not touched.

strata.rule: fixed before the run, from each task's reward basis in tau2's task file (not from any outcome)
strata.use: every outcome is reported for all 12 tasks and for each stratum. The gate is on all 12 tasks, as in H007: the strata are descriptive.

arm_order_rule: H007's schedule unchanged, with the treatment arm renamed: each (task, attempt) group runs both arms back to back; groups sorted by sha256('H007-order:' + task + ':' + attempt); the first arm alternates along that order and a task's two attempts use opposite orders. Times first: {'baseline': 12, 'harness_v3_1': 12}.
settings_note: Unchanged from H005/H006/H007: gpt-5-mini medium reasoning, 16,384 output tokens (incl. reasoning), gpt-5.2 low customer, alltools, seed 300, max_steps 200, billed budget accounting. Identical in both arms.

infrastructure.shared_by_both_arms: bench/sandbox_policy.py: shell reads denied outside the knowledge base (home, /tmp, system temp, both repositories); sandboxes under /private/var/tmp/aep_kb_sandboxes; the shell's environment reduced to an allow-list (no credentials). Validated: research/alltools/containment_check.json (canaries; every probe denied, knowledge base readable). Each trace records sandbox_policy and a shell_audit.
infrastructure.offline_validation: tests/test_alltools_compat.py, tests/test_alltools_e2e.py (scripted, fake embeddings, conclusive answer independence in both arms); reference controls under alltools 30/30 same reward, 0 hard-check firings (research/harness_v1/reference_controls_alltools.json)

budget_accounting_note: bench/budget.py 'billed': every call is still RESERVED conservatively (input bound at the full input price + max output); a completed call is SETTLED at the provider-billed cost from its own usage report, cached prompt tokens at the cached rate (full price when there is no cached rate or report, e.g. embeddings); unresolved calls hold their whole reservation. The upper bound (all prompt tokens at the full price) is still reported for every run; it may be about 3x the billed figure.
dense_retrieval: verified by the H005 preflight (research/alltools/dense_check.json: top-3 hit rate 0.867, $0.022); the document embeddings are cached and reused. Not repeated.
offline_evidence: research/v3_1/README.md: 7 tests (tests/test_harness_v3_1.py); reference controls 30/30 same reward under bm25 and alltools, 0 hard-check firings (research/harness_v1/reference_controls_v3.1*.json). v3's evidence carries over unchanged (research/v3/README.md): capability-search replay reaches the account-lookup document in 81/90 conversations that need it. NOT shown offline: what gpt-5-mini does after the new hold text; only a live run can show that.

outcomes.primary: official tau2 reward per conversation (48): passes per arm over complete pairs (of 24), and paired outcome per (task, attempt)
supporting: which tasks the gains and regressions come from
retrieval from each model's view (bench/kb_evidence.py): required-document recall at 'full' and 'full or partial'; whether the account-lookup document was reached when required
capability searches in v3.1: which triggers fired, whether a lookup tool was then called, and drafts not sent
progress with bench/metrics.py buckets (discoverable writes, discoverable reads, base writes, customer actions); agent read calls, attempted and successful writes
transfers and capability denials; harness held / released / withheld by check
cost per conversation and per pass, billed and upper bound; latency; agent input and output tokens
shell use and shell_audit flags per arm (any flag inspected before results are reported)
transfers against a should-transfer label (the task's reference actions include a transfer): wanted transfers made, unwanted transfers, per arm
held transfers in v3.1: how many, whether a transfer was executed later, and whether the agent told the customer a transfer was under way with none executed (read from the model's view)
same-code control: attempt 0 against attempt 1 within each arm (pass counts and per-task agreement)
all required documents reached per conversation, beside mean required-document recall
funnel per v3.1 conversation: capability search fired -> account-lookup document surfaced -> lookup tool offered -> lookup tool called -> write executed

safety_audit.scope: blind to arm, H002 codebook: every conversation with an executed write, both arms, plus both conversations of every (task, attempt) pair whose pass/fail differs
safety_audit.procedure: as H004: one first review for all scoped conversations; an independent second review for every flagged conversation plus the 4 unflagged ones with the most writes; disputes adjudicated blind before unblinding; any rule-dependent count reported under both readings; dispute counts are recounted from the executed writes and the customer's records, not from what the agent said (file_credit_card_transaction_dispute_4829 enforces no limit itself)
safety_audit.counts: confirmed violating actions and conversations with at least one, per arm; ambiguous separately

outcomes.not_evidence: 12 development tasks selected as solvable by strong agents, x 2 attempts, one model: a development screening result on an easier-than-average subset. Not an estimate of the benchmark score, not held-out, not leaderboard-comparable (the protocol is all 97 tasks x 4 trials).

decision_rule: An engineering screening gate fixed before the run (not a significance test). Take harness v3.1 forward to a held-out evaluation plan only if ALL hold on complete pairs: (1) harness_v3_1 passes at least 5 more of 24 than baseline; (2) counting each task once, more tasks improve than regress by at least 3; (3) safety screen: neither confirmed violating actions nor conversations with a confirmed violation are higher for harness_v3_1 under the adjudicated reading (any rule-dependent count reported under both readings). An exact paired sign test is reported beside the gate as a description. Success and cost are always reported together. If the gate is not met, the result is reported and v3.1 is not re-tuned on these tasks. ADDED in H008, before any run: (4) budget censoring: if any conversation is interrupted by its per-run cap, conditions (1) and (2) must ALSO hold with every cap-interrupted conversation counted as a failure and its pair kept; the number of cap interruptions per arm is reported. (5) scoring: every conversation counts once; nothing is scored as best of two attempts. A gate that is not met is reported as 'insufficient evidence at this size', not as 'no effect'.
noise_floor: research/literature/checks.py (gate_sim, 100,000 simulations per row; conversations independent given a task's pass probability). Two IDENTICAL agents differ by 3 or more passes of 24 in 29-40% of runs, and meet conditions (1) and (2) together in 3-6%. A true gain of +0.15 on every task meets them in 36-38%; +0.25 in 65-71%; +0.40 in 90-95%.

forecast_usd.basis: H005 billed (cache-aware) per conversation: standard mean $0.11, harness_v1 mean $0.14 (max $0.25). v3 adds up to 3 harness searches of 5+5 documents. These 12 tasks have fewer reference actions than the pilot set (median 4 vs 11).
forecast_usd.expected: about 5.00-8.00 billed for 48 conversations (the upper bound will read roughly 3x higher)

execution.budget_handling: Enforced on the BILLED figure (bench/budget.py): per_run_cap_usd ($0.75) is both each conversation's reservation from the total and its own enforced budget; $9.00 is the enforced total. If mean billed spend exceeds about $0.16 per conversation, the last runs may not start.
execution.incomplete: interrupted runs keep their outcome and are not rerun; unfunded runs are not_run, never failures, never replaced; incomplete pairs are excluded from the gate, which is evaluated on complete pairs with the count stated; the batch is labelled COMPLETE or INCOMPLETE.
execution.interruption: operator-stopped runs are journaled with their spend and the reason, and may rerun, disclosed
execution.approval: runs only after Nidhi approves in chat with the amount: 'run H008 with $9.00' (billed estimate; the upper bound is reported too)

no_retries: no conversation is repeated; every scheduled run is reported
